Book correction: Part (iii) asks for the derivative at t = 0, but there the \hat{j}-component \frac{\sin(t^2)}{t} becomes \frac{0}{0}: \mathbf{r}(0) does not exist, and a function must be defined at a point before it can have a derivative there. So, strictly as printed, \mathbf{r}'(0) does not exist. The gap is only a removable "hole", since \lim_{t \to 0}\frac{\sin(t^2)}{t} = 0. Giving the \hat{j}-component the v
